items.followUp: How is bioinformatics used to analyse biological data?

rubric.why: Identifies the computer or information-technology component of bioinformatics.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming computers or information technology as part of bioinformatics.

rubric.why: Specifies that the information being handled is biological.
rubric.description: Connects computer use with biological data or information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning biological data or information.

modelAnswer: Bioinformatics is the use of computers and information technology to store, retrieve and analyse biological data.

items.followUp: What does systematics study besides the diversity of organisms?

rubric.why: Identifies the diversity or variety of organisms as part of systematics.
rubric.description: States that systematics studies the diversity of organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning organismal diversity or variety.

rubric.why: Includes the relationships among organisms, another central part of systematics.
rubric.description: States that systematics studies relationships among organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning relationships among organisms.

modelAnswer: Systematics is the study of the diversity of organisms and their relationships.

items.followUp: Name the two main stages of the cell cycle.

rubric.why: Defines the cell cycle as an ordered sequence of events.
rubric.description: States that the cell cycle is a sequence or series of events.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a sequence or series of events.

rubric.why: Identifies the interval from a cell's formation until it divides.
rubric.description: States that the cycle runs from cell formation to cell division.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying cell formation and division as the beginning and end of the cycle.

modelAnswer: The cell cycle is the sequence of events from the formation of a cell until it divides into two daughter cells.

items.followUp: What is the role of lysosomes in autolysis?

rubric.why: States that lysosomes release their digestive enzymes during necrosis.
rubric.description: Mentions the release of enzymes from lysosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that lysosomes release or discharge enzymes, or burst and release them.

rubric.why: Describes the effect of the released enzymes on the cell.
rubric.description: States that the enzymes digest or break down the cell or its components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing digestion or breakdown of the cell or its components.

modelAnswer: During necrosis, lysosomes burst and release digestive enzymes.
These enzymes digest the cell's components, causing the cell to break down.

items.followUp: What is an enzyme's active site?

rubric.why: Identifies substrates as substances or reactants on which enzymes act.
rubric.description: Defines substrates as the substances or reactants acted upon by enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying substrates as the substances or reactants on which enzymes act.

rubric.why: Adds the role of the substrate in enzyme action: it binds at the active site or is converted to products.
rubric.description: States that substrates bind to an enzyme's active site or are converted into products.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning binding at the active site or conversion into products.

modelAnswer: Substrates are the reactants on which enzymes act.
They bind to an enzyme's active site and are converted into products.
